nodes.description: Heterozygous truncating, splice and missense CNOT3 variants reduce the amount of functional CNOT3. Patient blood shows reduced CNOT3 mRNA and altered expression of other CCR4-NOT subunits. CNOT3 is a non-catalytic subunit; its C terminus binds the rest of the complex, and loss of CNOT3 lowers the level of the CNOT1 scaffold, so its molecular role is to hold the deadenylase complex together rather than to catalyse deadenylation.

nodes.description: During cortical development, mRNA stability is tuned so that transcripts rising across development are stable and falling ones are labile. Complete Cnot3 loss in mouse neural progenitors alters progenitor fate and triggers p53-dependent apoptosis, with severe microcephaly and loss of deep-layer neurons. Heterozygous loss leaves mouse brain size normal, so the human phenotype is assumed to reflect a subtler, dosage-sensitive disturbance of the same process.

nodes.description: CNOT3 is required for CCR4-NOT complex integrity and for efficient poly(A) tail shortening and decay of target mRNAs. Reduced CNOT3 is expected to lengthen poly(A) tails and stabilise transcripts that should be cleared as cells change state. This step is established in mouse embryonic stem cells and progenitors; it has not been measured in patient neural tissue.
